title: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
data_curation: Training and eval data are fully self-generated via MCTS over three interactive environments on the AgentGym platform: WebShop (300 simulations, web shopping), ScienceWorld (200, text-based science tasks), and TextCraft (200, Minecraft crafting). MCTS collects pairs of bad and good trajectories sharing a common initial prefix; good/bad are separated by reward gap beta=0.2 and a quality lower bound alpha that rises across iterations (0.5 -> 0.7 -> 1.0), pushing good trajectories toward optimal. This yields thousands of revision+good pairs per env per iteration (e.g., WebShop iter3: 9000 revision / 2000 good; TextCraft iter3: 8000/4000). Ten hand-written revision-thought templates splice bad prefixes to good suffixes. No human or expert-model annotation is used. Following AgentTuning, agent data is mixed with ShareGPT (general corpus) at ratio eta=0.2. Test sets: 200 (WebShop), 200 (SciWorld), 100 (TextCraft).
curriculum: A two-phase iterative self-training loop repeated for three iterations. Phase I (Model-Guided Reflection Trajectory Generation) re-collects MCTS revision trajectories using the current actor; Phase II runs iterative SFT on the mixed good+revision+general data. The curriculum is encoded by the rising alpha threshold (0.5 -> 0.7 -> 1.0), so good trajectories progressively converge to optimal and the actor learns to revise earlier (weaker-to-stronger) errors within its current capability. Epochs are 3 in iteration 1 (cold-start) and 1 afterward to avoid overfitting; LR 2e-5, 3% warmup, cosine schedule, AdamW, seq len 8192, grad-clip 1, 8x A100-80GB. Multi-task training across all three environments consistently beats single-task, especially in later iterations, motivating joint data mixing.
method: Agent-R is an iterative self-training framework giving LLM agents on-the-fly reflection in POMDP-style interactive environments (ReAct prompting). Four trajectory types are defined: initial, bad, good, and revision. A revision trajectory splices a bad prefix up to a transition point t' with a good suffix that shares the same MCTS parent, joined by a revision signal rs (an 'Assistant: [reflection] / Human: OK.' marker sampled from 10 templates). The key contribution is model-guided transition-point determination: the actor itself identifies the first erroneous action within its current capability and truncates there, enabling timely revision rather than the Direct-Revision baseline that appends the good path only at trajectory end (t'=Tb). MCTS uses UCT (c_uct=0.25), k=8 rollouts, depth 20, 4 candidate actions per node, temperature 1. Training objective is a weighted SFT loss (Eq. 6): eta*{E_good[log pi(tau^g|u)] + E_rev[log pi(rs, tau(t>t')|u, tau(t<=t'))]} + (1-eta)*E_general[log pi(y|x)], with eta=0.2. This avoids expert supervision, mitigates cold-start, and reduces dead loops.
eval_metrics: Backbone is Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Metrics: average final reward for WebShop and SciWorld, success rate for TextCraft; max 100 rounds (50 in the revision-recovery setting). Baselines include closed-source models (GPT-3.5/4-Turbo/4o, Claude-3 Haiku/Sonnet, DeepSeek-Chat), open-source agents (Llama2-Chat-13B, AgentLM-7B/13B, Agent-FLAN), ETO (SFT then DPO on good/bad pairs), and a Direct-Revision ablation. Headline: Agent-R (iter3) averages 70.71 (WebShop 63.91, SciWorld 70.23, TextCraft 78.00) vs Direct-Revision 62.36 and ETO 65.12, a +5.59% gain over baselines and ahead of GPT-4o. In the revision-recovery benchmark Agent-R reaches 46.75 avg vs Direct-Revision 35.67. Ablations show revision trajectories beat self-generated optimal ones, adding only good trajectories to optimal hurts, average revision length shrinks across iterations (e.g., TextCraft 8.3 -> 4.7 -> 2.6), and repeat-action loops decline.
key_results: Llama-3.1-8B + Agent-R (iter 3) averages 70.71 across WebShop/SciWorld/TextCraft (63.91 / 70.23 / 78.00), beating Direct-Revision (62.36), ETO (65.12), and GPT-4o, a +5.59% gain. Revision trajectories outperform self-generated optimal trajectories, and average revision length drops across iterations (TextCraft 8.3 -> 2.6), indicating earlier, more reliable error detection.
evolution_note: Agent-R extends MCTS-driven agent training (e.g., Agent Q) and self-correction RL (SCoRe) by reacting against behavior cloning from all-correct expert trajectories, which cannot recover from errors in long-horizon interactive tasks. In the 2025 self-improving-agent wave, it motivates automatic step-level reflection-data construction and iterative self-play SFT without human or expert-model supervision.
